_expect.name: Ashes to Ashes/ Bridge of Immortals Area

nh_ashes_to_ashes_bridge_of_immortals_ar.blurb: A small cluster of twelve boulder problems below the Devil's Den cliffband in Pawtuckaway State Park. It is pure bouldering on scattered blocks of varied size, including some big, tall ones. The spread is wide for so few problems: a handful of moderates around V3 to V4, a few V5 and V6 lines, and a top end reaching V8 and V9, so it suits stronger climbers more than beginners. Tall, committing problems are part of the appeal here. Most of the Den was developed decades ago and has seen modest traffic since, so expect moss, lichen and some fallen trees around the easier lines. Bring several pads and a spotter.

nh_no_money_down_left.blurb: The far-left stretch of The Meadows at Rumney, a low-angle face only about 45 feet high that sits right by the parking area. Nearly all of the twelve routes are bolted sport lines, with a single trad climb mixed in. Grades run from the 5.7 range up to the low 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.10 band, so it works for climbers stepping up to harder sport as well as those who just want a quick warm-up. The wall is short, popular and often busy, and the approach is only a few minutes.

nh_center_section.blurb: The middle stretch of The Meadows at Rumney, a short walk from the parking lot. Of the twelve routes, ten are bolted sport lines and two are trad. The grades are friendly for the most part: a couple of easy 5.5-range leads, a good number of 5.8 to 5.10 sport routes, and one standout much harder at the top end, around 5.13. That makes it one of the better places at Rumney to build mileage on moderate steep-ish rock. The Meadows as a whole stays shaded in summer, but it is popular, so expect company on weekends.

nh_slab_wall_the.blurb: A roughly 70-foot wall at Devil's Den in New Durham, in the Lakes Region, and one of the first cliffs you reach on the walk up. As the name says, the climbing is steep-ish slab, with a few arete lines mixed in. Of the twelve routes most are trad, with a few bolted sport lines and one top-rope. Grades sit mostly between 5.7 and 5.10, with the largest group at 5.9, so it is a good pick for climbers working on slab technique at a moderate level. The wall is tall for the area and draws the most visitors at the Den; it also builds ice in winter.

nh_outback_wall_the.blurb: One of the cliffs at Devil's Den in New Durham, in the Lakes Region, reached by passing the Land of Overhangs and bearing left at the trail forks. The rock quality is excellent and the setting is attractive, with technical face climbing on steep walls. Of the twelve climbs, five are sport routes, three are trad and four are boulder problems from roughly V1 to V5. The roped grades run from 5.9 into the 5.11 range, centred on 5.10, so it is geared to climbers comfortable leading in the 5.10s. Several of the area's best-known lines are found here.

nh_fisher_block.blurb: A big boulder in the Zig Zag Area of the Black Jack Boulders at Rumney, with a second giant block just behind it. It holds twelve problems, all bouldering, spread from the very easiest grades through the middle V grades up to a couple of V9 and V10 lines. Two problems on the main block are the draw, while there are also quieter lines and a gentle option for newer boulderers. The boulders stand in the woods in the Black Jack cluster, which is buggy in summer and best on cool, dry days.
nh_fisher_block.approach: Head west on the main trail from the Entrance Boulders, past the leaning Umbrella Boulder, down a short dip and up beyond the Dill Bundle. The two large blocks stand on the right side of the trail just beyond.
